2.8.4 Future Expansion. System should have scalability provision for addition of further 03 fixed and 06 handsfree positions in future.
2.8.5 MTBF should be more than 30000 Hrs, while MTTR less than 15 min.
2.8.6 Helmets. The helmet should have following features:
2.8.6.1 It should be impact resistant and should provide protection against burns due to flash.
2.8.6.2 It should provide electric shock protection.
2.8.6.3 It should have integrated glare visors to provide sun, wind and dust protection.
2.8.6.4 Should be fire protection and NBC clothing compatible.
2.8.7 Headphones. The headphones should have following features:
2.8.7.1 It should be integrated with wireless based communication equipment through noise cancelling microphones.
2.8.8 Security of Transmission. System should be of low power to ensure minimum radiation. Power level should be HERO and HERP safe for use on helo deck during refueling and ammunition.

Portable Units. 3.4.1 Helmet may be corded with max cord length of 6ft. 3.4.2 System should be cordless. 3.4.3 Mobile units should be compact, lightweight and powered by rechargeable batteries with following usable time:- Stand by time - 12 hrs or more. Talk mode - 02 hrs or more.
At least 04 battery sets should be provided for each mobile user.
At least 02 battery charging stations with provision to simultaneously charge batteries for up to all 16 mobile users should be supplied as part of equipment.
Fixed. Units should have both inbuilt speakers and pluggable headsets.
Reliability. The system should have full redundancy in terms of failure of Base Station and Switch.
Lifting Arrangements. Units weighing more than 40 Kgs shall be provided with collar eyebolts or suitable lifting lugs/arrangements.
Terminal. Bolted type terminal and crimped socket of electrolytic copper are to be provided for all incoming and outgoing cables.
Anti-condensation Heating. Wherever necessary, equipment shall be provided with anti-condensation heating elements, which are to be switched on automatically when the equipment is switched off.
Safety Standards. All units to be provided with earthing bolts. Each unit which is connected to ships mains are to be provided with fuse protection.
Cabinet Cooling. Sufficient cooling and circulation of air should be provided for the system cabinets.
Mounting Arrangement. The equipment would be mounted on shock mounts onboard ship.
Power supply - 230V/115V, 1 phase, 50/60 Hz, System should also have provision for operating on 24V DC supply in case of emergency.
Freq range – V/UHF 100-400 Mhz. Channels – At least 03 channels catering for 16 wireless positions.
Priorities - Priorities of positions in HDCS would be as follows: I- LSO, II- CFD, III- Bridge/Ops room, IV- Hangar. Rest of the positions can be put on the lowermost rung of hierarchy.
Switching between channels is to be provided.
System should be capable of handsfree operation on helo deck and hangar.

Warning Indications. 4.6.1 Suitable audio, visual and vibrate warning should be available to warn user of incoming calls when on different channel. 4.6.2 Audio and visual warning for low battery should be provided.

Recording. The system should have recording facility with the following provisions: 4.7.1 Record and playback of all Helo deck and aviation related communications. 4.7.2 Recording and replay facilities of all channels for at least 24-hrs with time tags and should be transferable to secondary storage devices like CDs and DVDs. 4.7.3 The format of recording should be of that type that can be replayed in COTS device or PCs. It should be able to synchronise the timings of helo deck CCTV system.
BITE. The system should have capability for on line and off-line maintenance diagnostics.
Interface. Supplier is responsible for interfacing and integration of HDCS with following ship system: 4.9.1 VCS Mk III; 4.9.2 Main broadcast; 4.9.3 Aviation broadcast.
